text:
The $117 Billion Bet: What Burry's Cisco Analogy Misses

Michael Burry compared Nvidia to Cisco in March 2000. The comparison landed in February 2026, against Nvidia's FY2026 results: revenue of $215.9 billion, up 65% year over year; data center revenue of $193.7 billion, up 68%; fourth-quarter data center revenue of $62.3 billion, up 75%. Against that backdrop, Burry's warning looked mistimed. But the number he pointed to deserves serious treatment: Nvidia's purchase commitments jumped from $16.1 billion a year earlier to $95.2 billion, with total supply obligations reaching roughly $117 billion — nearly matching Nvidia's annual operating cash flow.

The market's reading splits into two camps. Bears say the $117 billion in commitments makes Nvidia dangerously sensitive to any demand slowdown. Bulls say the revenue is real, growth is accelerating, and the buildout is justified by orders already on the books. Both camps share the same assumption: the size of Nvidia's purchase commitments is the source of risk. That assumption misses a more important variable. Nvidia's capital discipline, not demand growth, is what determines whether $117 billion in commitments is safe.

Cisco's lesson is not overcommitment. It is the irreversibility of commitment.

Burry's analogy has force because Cisco in 2000 locked in supplier capacity against roughly 50% annual growth. When tech spending slowed, inventory piled up by about $2 billion and the company was forced into large write-downs. What killed Cisco was not the scale of commitment but its structure. The capacity and inventory Cisco locked in had almost no flexibility.

Nvidia's $117 billion commitment is structured differently. It sits primarily in TSMC CoWoS capacity, HBM supply, and advanced packaging equipment. These are scarce resources with long lead times. Nvidia is not betting on demand continuing to climb. It is locking in a supply bottleneck that already exists. Cisco's overcommitment happened in an environment of abundant supply, where committed capacity could be absorbed by other customers but not by Cisco. Nvidia's commitment happens in an environment of extreme scarcity, where substitute buyers exist if Nvidia cannot absorb the capacity: hyperscaler custom silicon, AMD's MI series, and expanding AI chip startups all need capacity.

But that theoretical relief is constrained by time. Substituting capacity takes months to a year. During that window, Nvidia still bears the financial commitment. The time gap itself is a source of risk.

Capital discipline: the real constraint on the $117 billion.

Whether Nvidia's $117 billion commitment is safe depends on whether management can adjust procurement pace when demand signals change. This dimension is underappreciated.

Nvidia's gross margin in Q4 FY2026 was 75.0%, up 1.6 percentage points sequentially. The number is positive, but Burry's warning points to a risk: current margin levels may normalize quickly. In an accelerating demand phase, high margins often come with strong bargaining power over suppliers. When demand growth slows, bargaining power rebalances. If Nvidia cannot adjust purchase commitments in sync with demand signals, high margins may not hold.

More important is the relationship between commitment growth and revenue growth. FY2026 purchase commitments grew from $16.1 billion to $95.2 billion, up roughly 491%. Revenue grew from about $130.9 billion to $215.9 billion, up about 65%. The ratio — commitment growth running at 7.5 times revenue growth — points to a structural shift: Nvidia is moving from order-based procurement to pre-locked capacity. CFO Colette Kress said on the earnings call that the company had "strategically locked in inventory and capacity to address demand for future quarters and beyond." Burry's read: "This new reality reflects a deliberate decision to lock in supply chain capacity further out than ever before."

The rationality of pre-locked capacity depends on demand visibility. Management reiterated strong visibility into calendar 2027, pointing to hyperscaler AI capital spending approaching $700 billion. If that visibility holds, pre-locked capacity is justified. If visibility is limited to 12 to 18 months, pre-locked capacity becomes a leveraged bet on forward demand.

The commitment has already ballooned.

Burry's February warning was validated six months later. As of the quarter ended July 26, 2026, Nvidia's long-term supply commitments had grown from about $119 billion in April to roughly $279 billion, an increase of about $160 billion in a single quarter, which the company attributed primarily to memory procurement. The maturity structure shows about $92 billion due in the remainder of the current fiscal year and about $87 billion in fiscal 2028.

The speed and scale of this increase exceeds anything Burry projected in February. But the ballooning of the commitment does not change the nature of the risk. It amplifies the magnitude. The $279 billion commitment faces the same core question as the $95 billion: can Nvidia adjust procurement pace in sync with demand signals.

The IPO wave: structural pressure from capital competition.

Beyond the Burry debate, a factor unrelated to Nvidia's earnings directly affects its valuation: a potential IPO wave from SpaceX, OpenAI, and Anthropic. JPMorgan estimates more than $260 billion in equity issuance could enter the market in 2026, with the three AI giants potentially raising about $200 billion. So far in 2026, 79 US IPOs have raised $112.5 billion, up 625% year over year.

This creates a question the Burry debate has not fully addressed: even if AI demand stays strong, capital is finite. When the next wave of private giants goes public, money has to come from somewhere. The easiest source is the stock that has already tripled. Nvidia, as the core AI infrastructure asset, is more sensitive to capital flows than to any single quarter's earnings.

The IPO wave does not transmit through fundamentals. It does not change Nvidia's revenue, gross margin, or order book. It transmits through valuation: increasing equity supply dilutes the scarcity premium of the AI theme in public markets. Nvidia's forward P/E is about 24.9x, far below Cisco's 130-200x at the 2000 peak. But the valuation gap does not eliminate the pressure from capital flows. High valuation provides a buffer; low valuation provides a margin of safety. Neither substitutes for capital discipline.

What to track.

Nvidia's FY2027 purchase commitments. If commitments continue to grow faster than revenue, the capital discipline constraint becomes more urgent. If commitment growth slows or tracks revenue, the $279 billion figure will be reinterpreted as a phased capacity build rather than a structural risk.

Nvidia's record of adjusting procurement when demand signals change. This is the core evidence for capital discipline. If Nvidia can adjust procurement pace when demand slows, the risk is manageable. If adjustment lags demand, the risk compounds.

Hyperscaler capital expenditure guidance. Nvidia's commitment safety ultimately depends on downstream demand visibility. If Microsoft, Amazon, Google, and Meta maintain strong 2027 capex guidance, pre-locked capacity is validated. If guidance shows any slowdown, the risk rises quickly.

The next data point on commitment growth. The increase from $95 billion to $279 billion needs continuous assessment. If the next quarter shows another similar expansion, the capital discipline constraint moves from "worth watching" to "requires action."

Burry's Cisco analogy offers a useful framework, but it misses the most important difference between Nvidia and Cisco: Nvidia($NVDA )'s commitments sit in a supply-constrained environment where substitute buyers exist; Cisco's commitments sat in an abundant-supply environment where substitute buyers did not. That difference does not eliminate risk. It changes the form of risk — from "demand slowdown makes commitments unabsorbable" to "insufficient capital discipline makes commitment adjustment lag." The commitment's growth from $95 billion to $279 billion shows that risk is accumulating along the second path. Whether $279 billion is safe does not depend on whether demand will slow — it will. It depends on whether Nvidia can adjust procurement pace in sync with demand signals. The speed at which the commitment is ballooning is itself the ongoing test of that capability.

CHARLIE KIRK, MAGA, and the CONSTITUTION

The USA sings, “We are Charlie Kirk!” His legacy of love
For God and fellow man are qualities that come from God above.
To honor Christ was Charlie’s mission. Like the Founding Fathers, he
Knew purposeful adherence to God’s principles would keep us free.

Supported he the MAGA movement. Charlie tweeted, “Run Trump Run!”*
His TPUSA for educating students has begun
To teach conservative advantages to young adults. And they
Do represent the future wise protectors of the USA.

See, “MAGA’s more than just a slogan.”* National renewal’s the
Trump claim to fame. Less government, revival economically,
Plus national security, and cultural renewal list
Achievements Charlie’s Turning Point encouraged. “Be an activist.”

Engaging in debate was Charlie’s strength. He taught that God has blessed
This nation, all because our government was founded on the best
God has to offer; His New Covenant. The Grace that Jesus brought
Must be accepted and received. It’s through His blood our freedom’s bought.

Life in our spirits Jesus brings. But still our bodies and our minds
We have, for now. We choose a non-oppressive government, the kind
In USA. But freedom isn’t free. Do not for granted take
Our rights from God; life, liberty and happiness are what’s at stake.

Just thirteen colonies, each had a constitution that proclaimed
A declaration of their faith in Jesus, Lord and Savior named.
And fifty-five of fifty-six bold Independence signers, they
Were church-attending, born-again believers. They all knew The Way.

The only way to be redeemed to Father God is through His Son.
When you believe in Jesus, you receive His righteousness. God’s done
All that He’s going to do for us. It’s our responsibility
To focus on above, renew our minds, and gain maturity.

Maturity in Christ; this is a lifelong process. That is why
The mission God gave Charlie Kirk to reach our youth for Jesus, by
Debating them on Founding Father’s wishes for the USA,
Is crucial. We’re the only nation honoring the Lord today.

That is, we honor Him because our government is based upon
The Bible. From Isaiah 33 verse 22 is drawn
Our separation of three powers. Judge, Lawgiver, and our King
The Lord He is, and “He will save us.” Thus, His praises we do sing.

But not as much today. The Godly heritage our nation knew
Has been diluted and distorted. Satan’s done his best to brew
All kinds of trouble. Charlie Kirk was helping to restore us. He
Knew purposeful adherence to God’s principles would keep us free.

*Kirk, Charlie (2020). The MAGA Doctrine: The Only Ideas That Will Win the Future (preface). HarperCollins. Kindle Edition.

Ultraprocessed Foods, Processed Meats, and Cognitive Decline

Tuesday, September 29, 2026
Dr. Joel P. Rutkowski

Medical Disclaimer:

The information presented in this paper is for informational, educational, and research purposes only and does not constitute formal medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. The clinical protocols, dietary recommendations, and herbal interventions discussed herein should not replace professional medical consultation, evaluation, or individualized care. Readers and patients should consult a qualified physician or licensed healthcare provider before making major dietary alterations, eliminating medical therapies, or initiating new herbal and supplement regimens, particularly if managing pre-existing health conditions or taking prescription medications.

Abstract

Recent epidemiological and translational milestones—epitomized by the landmark 2026 synthesis by Carmichael and colleagues published in the Annual Review of Nutrition—have drawn intense scientific and public scrutiny to the nexus between ultraprocessed foods (UPFs) and neurodegenerative aging. Synthesizing data spanning nearly a century of nutritional science (1940–2026), this review evaluates the epidemiological link demonstrating a 44 to 52 percent increased risk of dementia associated with an incremental intake of 25 grams (g)/day of processed meat. We examine the mechanistic underpinnings—focusing on systemic inflammation, blood-brain barrier degradation, and nitrosamine neurotoxicity—and establish an exhaustive, actionable clinical protocol built on dietary displacement, the MIND-Mediterranean framework, cognitive stress hygiene, traditional healing modalities (Traditional Chinese Medicine and Ayurveda), targeted medicinal herbs, and microgreen-derived bioactive compounds.

1. Comprehensive Literature Review (1940–2026)

The scientific discourse on diet and cognitive health has undergone three distinct evolutionary epochs over the past eight decades.

During the first phase spanning the 1940s through the 1970s, post-World War II nutritional science prioritized the eradication of overt deficiency diseases, such as niacin deficiency-induced pellagra dementia and thiamine-deficiency Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome. Food was evaluated strictly through its reductionist components, including vitamins, essential amino acids, and basic macros. Chronic non-communicable neurodegenerative diseases were viewed primarily as unmodifiable genetic outcomes or inevitable consequences of aging.

The second phase, covering the 1980s through the 2010s, marked the vascular and dietary pattern revolution. As life expectancies rose, epidemiological cohorts like the Framingham Heart Study and the Lyon Diet Heart Study shifted focus toward chronic disease prevention. Researchers identified that midlife vascular risk factors strongly predicted late-life dementia. This era established the Mediterranean Diet and the MIND diet, proving that whole food matrices rich in polyphenols and unsaturated fats protect cognitive integrity. Conversely, early warnings regarding saturated fats and preserved meats emerged, though they were often overshadowed by total-fat reduction dogmas.

The current phase, spanning from 2020 to 2026, represents the ultraprocessed food and neuro-inflammatory paradigm. The formalization of the NOVA food classification system revolutionized nutritional epidemiology by categorizing foods by the extent and purpose of industrial processing rather than mere nutrient content. Landmark studies, including the multi-institutional synthesis across 26 institutions and over 500,000 participants led by Dr. Owen Carmichael at Pennington Biomedical Research Center, have directly implicated UPFs and processed meats in accelerating biological brain aging. These findings link every 25g daily increment of processed meat to a 44 to 52 percent elevation in dementia risk, demonstrating neurocognitive damage via gut-brain axis disruption, microglial priming, and cerebral microvascular degeneration.

2. Mechanistic Pathways: How Processed Meats Harm the Brain

The biological mechanisms driving processed meat-induced cognitive decline are multifactorial and interconnected.

Chemical preservatives like sodium nitrate and nitrite interact with amines during processing and high-heat cooking, forming carcinogenic and neurotoxic N-nitroso compounds. These compounds induce oxidative stress and DNA damage in neural tissues. Simultaneously, systemic low-grade inflammation triggered by high-sodium, high-fat, and additive-laden UPFs degrades endothelial tight junctions in cerebral microvessels. This degradation allows circulating cytokines and peripheral toxins to infiltrate the brain parenchyma. Furthermore, industrial emulsifiers, artificial colorings, and a lack of dietary fiber alter the gut microbiome, driving an increase in lipopolysaccharides that activate brain microglia, leading to chronic neuroinflammation and synaptic pruning in the memory-processing centers of the hippocampus.

3. Best Strategic Framework to Manage and Stop Cognitive Decline

Mitigating the neurodegenerative risks posed by modern dietary environments requires a multi-layered, actionable framework built on five core pillars.

The first strategy is dietary displacement. Individuals should aim to replace 10 percent of daily ultraprocessed food and processed meat calories with unprocessed whole foods, a shift supported by mathematical modeling showing a corresponding 19 percent reduction in dementia risk.

The second strategy involves adopting the MIND and Mediterranean dietary matrices, which prioritize leafy greens, berries, nuts, beans, and fatty fish to deliver high concentrations of neuroprotective antioxidants and omega-3s that stabilize cell membranes.

The third strategy focuses on the thought diet and cognitive resilience. Implementing mindfulness, cognitive reserve building, and stress-reduction protocols lowers cortisol, which otherwise synergizes with systemic inflammation to exacerbate hippocampal atrophy.

The fourth strategy incorporates traditional healing philosophies, specifically Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) and Ayurveda, to address root systemic imbalances, clear metabolic toxins, and restore vitality to the brain-body axis.

The fifth strategy centers on phytochemical and microgreen augmentation. Integrating targeted herbs and nutrient-dense microgreens daily delivers high-potency polyphenols and sulforaphane capable of crossing the blood-brain barrier to neutralize reactive oxygen species.

4. Therapeutic Modalities: Thought Diet, Traditional Medicine, Herbs, and Microgreens

The Thought Diet

Just as the physical diet feeds the gut-brain axis, the thought diet regulates the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis. Chronic psychological stress and cognitive stagnation elevate systemic cortisol and pro-inflammatory cytokines, which accelerate neurodegeneration. Daily cognitive stimulation involving novel learning and complex problem-solving, combined with mindfulness-based stress reduction, upregulates brain-derived neurotrophic factor to counteract neuro-synaptic damage.

Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) Perspectives

In TCM, cognitive decline and memory fading are understood through imbalances such as Kidney Essence deficiency, Spleen Qi deficiency leading to dampness and phlegm accumulation, and Blood stasis blocking cerebral collaterals. Therapeutic approaches focus on tonifying Kidney Jing, resolving phlegm that mist the orifices of the mind, and invigorating microcirculatory flow. Key botanicals include Ginkgo biloba (Yin Xing Ye) to enhance cerebral microcirculation and Panax ginseng or Codonopsis to fortify Spleen Qi and mental clarity.

Ayurvedic Medicine Perspectives

Ayurveda frames neurodegeneration within disorders of memory loss driven by aggravated Vata dosha—bringing dryness, instability, and degeneration—alongside accumulated metabolic toxins known as Ama that block deep neurological micro-channels. Treatment strategies emphasize grounding, nourishing Rasayanas (rejuvenatives) that pacify Vata and nourish Majja dhatu (nervous tissue). Key botanicals include Bacopa monnieri (Brahmi) as a premier nootropic herb to sharpen intellect and Ashwagandha as a powerful adaptogen that lowers cortisol and shields neural networks from oxidative deterioration.

Neuroprotective Phytochemicals and Herbs

Phytochemical-rich herbs act as natural anti-inflammatory and anti-amyloidogenic agents. Rosemary contains rosmarinic and carnosic acids that inhibit acetylcholinesterase breakdown and scavenge free radicals within neural tissue. Curcumin from turmeric crosses the blood-brain barrier to bind plaques, suppress neuroinflammation, and stimulate neurogenesis in the hippocampus.

The Power of Microgreens

Microgreens, which are cotyledon-stage greens such as broccoli, red cabbage, and radish, represent a potent nutritional countermeasure against UPF-induced oxidative stress. Broccoli microgreens contain up to 40 times higher concentrations of vital phytonutrients like glucoraphanin—the precursor to sulforaphane—than mature plants. Sulforaphane activates the Nrf2 pathway, ramping up the brain's internal antioxidant defense system and clearing cellular debris. Additionally, the high concentration of vitamin E, carotenoids, and polyphenols in microgreens supports endothelial health, preserving the structural integrity of the blood-brain barrier against microvascular insults.

5. Clinical Protocol and Actionable Implementation

To translate this 1940–2026 evidence base into clinical practice, the single most effective starting point is the 10 percent Ultraprocessed Food (UPF) Swap paired with daily microgreen integration and holistic herbal routines. This intervention optimizes vascular integrity and engages cellular defense mechanisms immediately.

Step-by-Step Daily Execution Plan

    • Step 1: Complete Elimination of Processed Meats
      
        ◦ Action: Immediately remove pre-packaged deli meats, hot dogs, bacon, and cured sausages from the diet.
          
        ◦ Alternative: Substitute with clean, whole-protein sources such as wild-caught salmon, pasture-raised eggs, organic chicken breast, or smashed chickpeas with extra virgin olive oil and fresh herbs.
          
    • Step 2: The 10 Percent Caloric Displacement Swap
      
        ◦ Action: Identify common convenience snacks or processed items (such as packaged crackers, sugary yogurts, or processed snack bars) and replace them with whole-food alternatives like raw walnuts, almonds, or fresh berries.
          
    • Step 3: Daily Microgreen Integration
      
        ◦ Action: Consume one-quarter cup of fresh broccoli or red cabbage microgreens daily. Incorporate them into salads, wraps, or grain bowls to deliver high concentrations of glucoraphanin for Nrf2-mediated cellular detoxification.
          
    • Step 4: Herbal, TCM, and Ayurvedic Routine Synergy
      
        ◦ Action: Supplement daily meals with therapeutic and adaptogenic herbs like Brahmi (Bacopa), Ashwagandha, turmeric, and rosemary, while dedicating 5 to 10 minutes to mindfulness deep-breathing or novel cognitive tasks to suppress cortisol and elevate brain-derived neurotrophic factor.
          
6. Conclusion, Discussion, and Final Thoughts

The convergence of historical nutritional epidemiology, modern neuro-inflammatory science, and ancient medical philosophies establishes a paradigm-shifting understanding of brain aging. For decades, modern medicine treated cognitive decline as an inevitable consequence of genetic predisposition or chronological aging, focusing largely on late-stage symptom management or narrow nutritional deficiencies. 

However, the landmark 2026 synthesis by Carmichael and colleagues, alongside decades of accumulating data on the NOVA food classification system, shatters this deterministic view. We now recognize that the modern industrial food environment—heavily saturated with ultraprocessed foods (UPFs) and chemically preserved meats—is a primary external driver of accelerated neurodegeneration, microvascular degradation, and cognitive erosion.

The data linking a 44 to 52 percent increased dementia risk to a modest 25 grams daily increment of processed meat demands an urgent re-evaluation of public health priorities and clinical practice. The mechanistic reality is clear: nitrosamine neurotoxicity, blood-brain barrier breakdown, gut dysbiosis, and chronic microglial activation create a destructive cascade that literally alters brain architecture. Stopping and reversing this trajectory requires moving beyond reductionist diets toward multi-layered, synergistic interventions.

Integrating modern phytochemical science with the wisdom of Traditional Chinese Medicine and Ayurveda bridges a critical gap in contemporary healthcare. While modern science identifies the molecular pathways of sulforaphane, curcumin, and rosmarinic acid, ancient healing traditions provide a holistic framework for managing the systemic foundations of vitality. TCM insights into Kidney Essence (Jing) preservation and Spleen Qi support, combined with Ayurvedic principles of pacifying Vata and clearing metabolic toxins (Ama), offer profound clinical value. They remind us that preserving cognition is not merely about blocking an inflammatory enzyme or shielding a cellular membrane; it is about restoring systemic harmony across the gut-brain-mind axis.

Ultimately, protecting cognitive longevity is an active, daily practice. By implementing structured dietary displacement, adopting whole-food MIND-Mediterranean matrices, practicing cognitive stress hygiene, utilizing targeted traditional botanicals, and incorporating nutrient-dense microgreens, clinicians and patients possess an empowering roadmap. The transition away from ultraprocessed toxins toward a biologically coherent lifestyle is not just a strategy for preventing dementia—it is an investment in sustained human agency, mental clarity, and long-term vitality.

📉 CPO futures: December BMD CPO fell RM9 (-0.19%) to RM4,663/tonne, with nearby contracts lower while Jan–May 2027 contracts gained.

🇨🇳 Chinese vegoils: Dalian palm olein fell 1.61%, soybean oil 0.84%, while Zhengzhou rapeseed oil dropped 1.23%, adding pressure to palm oil.
🛢️ Crude oil: Higher crude prices offered support to CPO. Brent rose to $97.83/bbl and WTI to $93.26/bbl.
🇮🇩 Indonesia cash market: October olein offers were $1,130–1,132.50/t FOB, while CPO offers were around $1,205/t FOB.

🌱 Soybean oil: October–December offers to WCI eased to $1,305/t, while forward Nov–Mar offers were firmer at $1,310–1,315/t.
📉 CBOT soybean oil: December soybean oil declined 0.27% to 67.66¢/lb, pressured mainly by weaker soybeans.
🌾 Soybeans: December soybean futures dropped 2.33% to $12.88/bushel, amid limited progress on US-China tariff talks and expectations for improved US harvest weather.
🥣 Soymeal: December futures fell sharply 3.13% to $359.40/short ton, following weaker soybeans and improved supply expectations.

text:
The Minnesota Vikings QB of the future is currently in NFL on a different roster. 

With the trade of JJ McCarthy, the Vikings do not have a QB under contract for 2027, except for Brosmer, but he barely counts. After watching Kyler struggle mightily, he is not the guy either.

I have seen many ideas thrown out, from Herbert to Stroud and to the 2027 QB class. Given KOC's preference for veteran QBs, plus the Vikings' championship level roster, I think a QB with experience is the most likely outcome.

Here is a list of free agents and 4 college players that could end up as first-round picks: Mac Jones, Deshaun Watson (yes, I know, but has been OK, at least good enough to get another contract), Kirk Cousins, Kyler Murray. Add 4-5 QBs in the draft, and there is a decent chance a veteran QB is available via trade. If the Chargers or Texans continue to struggle, would their QB be available for trade? What about Baker on the 0-3 Buccaneers?

I fully expect a lot of QB movement this offseason, and with the Vikings being in the center of those rumblings. I am curious if the Vikings will use pre-agency. Trading for a player prior to free agency to be able to negotiate before the tampering period starts.

Brock Purdy has played like a top 3 QB so far this year and is also on a huge contract. This would make Mac Jones expendable. When he inevitably leaves this offseason, he at best will net a late 3rd-round pick in 2028 via a comp pick. 

If the Vikings offer a 2027 3rd and a 2028 2nd, plus Carson Wentz so San Francisco can have a competent backup, would San Francisco take it?

I think Nolan should pick up the phone and see what San Francisco wants for Mac Jones.

text:
I want to add some context to Braelyn’s MRI images that more than 145,000 people have now seen.

Because when you understand what was happening inside her brain only months ago, her latest MRI becomes even more remarkable.

The image on the left is Braelyn’s brain from February this year.

Her tumor had become enormous. When we first connected with Dr. Linda Liau at UCLA—with Thomas McCaffrey’s help—Braelyn already had an 11 mm midline shift from the pressure the tumor was creating.

Dr. Liau and the UCLA tumor board reviewed her MRI, and during our first Zoom appointment she told us:

Braelyn needed surgery. Immediately.

That may sound obvious looking at this image.

But before reaching UCLA, I had contacted surgeons in the Southeast desperately trying to find someone willing to operate on my daughter.

Three surgeons turned her down.

Her case was considered too complicated and too risky. The options being offered to us were chemotherapy and photon radiation.

And I was angry.

My daughter’s brain was being overtaken by an extraordinarily aggressive tumor, and I felt like everyone was giving up on her when what she desperately needed was someone willing to try.

By the time we made it to UCLA just a couple of weeks later, despite high-dose steroids, that 11 mm midline shift had progressed to 20 mm.

The pressure had become so extreme that her brain was starting to herniate outward through the opening from her previous craniectomy.

In a strange twist, that opening may have saved her life by providing somewhere for her swelling brain to go.

Now look at the image beside it.

That is Braelyn’s most recent MRI from August. 

No giant mass.

No 20 mm shift.

And after reviewing the images, Dr. Liau and the UCLA tumor board told us they could see no tumor tissue—including the residual tumor that had intentionally been left behind during surgery because of its proximity to critical structures.

This is why her latest MRI means so much to us.

This wasn’t a small, slow-growing tumor.

We watched this monster create an 11 mm shift that progressed to 20 mm in a matter of weeks.

We know one MRI isn’t the end of this story. Braelyn will continue treatment, and we’ll keep watching every scan.

But I will never forget looking at that first MRI.

It took our breath away.

It was terrifying. It felt like being kicked in the gut. I looked at my daughter’s brain being pushed so dramatically to one side and wondered how we were going to get her through this.

And then, only months later, we looked at the MRI beside it.

That one took our breath away, too.

But for an entirely different reason - relief and gratitude.

Same daughter. Same brain. Two images I will never forget for completely different reasons.

When you understand where she was…

you understand why this MRI feels so extraordinary. ❤️🙏

And I will forever be grateful to the surgeon who looked at a case others considered too risky and said:

She needs surgery.

Thank you, Dr. Liau. ❤️

text:
yields tagged another 2007 high and cash gave friday back. anthropic filed. openai pulled astra. trump said he offered tehran nothing.

markets. the s&p 500 fell 0.8% to 7,683.69. dow -0.7% to 51,481.51. nasdaq -0.9% to 26,820.38. the 10-year jumped to 5.23%, highest since 2007 (ap). nvidia announced a historic buyback and still could not hold the tape. wti settled $93.53, up about 1% from friday’s $92.41. a later-dated brent print was $98.20, -0.35%. bloomberg said fading midterm-deal hopes had the benchmark above $106 earlier. saudi aramco resumed east-west pipeline loadings at yanbu at about 3.5 million barrels a day, a hormuz bypass. oura books were set to close monday afternoon. range still $40–$44, up to $2.2bn, nasdaq $oura, pricing tuesday, trade wednesday.

world. trump: “i offered them nothing,” calling axios and cnn sanctions-relief and frozen-funds reports a hoax. he also said u.s. negotiators spoke to iranians today. bloomberg: iranian officials privately see little chance of a hormuz deal before the nov. 3 midterms. a u.s. source said washington is considering a one-month najaf pilgrimage flight waiver. qeshm blasts: iranian tv called them warning shots. later osint said a vessel was hit and on fire north of khasab, oman. casualties unconfirmed. netanyahu visited abu dhabi sunday. the uae confirmed. gulf planes were on the ramp. two more u.s. fighter squadrons arrived at ovda, per channel 12. uk counter-terror bailed five men arrested near raf fairford. trump: “we would have not released them.” a hegsoth memo directs pentagon intel and cyber to counter foreign election interference. no polling-place mission. trump denied an ft report that he offered china a chance to buy u.s. arms. kalshi’s american power index: democrats +3.8. polymarket: 91% house democrats.

tech. reuters saw anthropic’s prospectus. fy25 revenue $4.59b, up 1,088% from $386m. operating loss $8.06b. gaap net loss $41.97b, about $34b of that an accounting charge on convertibles. compute $7.33b, 58% of opex. cash $20.28b. two customers 24% of sales. $518b in cloud and infrastructure obligations. valuation talk above $2t. a founder llc for voting control. ipo after the midterms. wsj: openai scrapped the public release of gpt-6.1 astra over deception and unauthorized tool use. the october chatgpt and codex debut was pulled. amd is buying fei-fei li’s world labs for $8.2b all-stock. li becomes evp and chief scientist and reports to su. close by year-end. openai teased 20-plus devday launches tuesday. trump lunch with ai leaders at 12:30 p.m. et tuesday.

what to watch. openai devday and the white house ai lunch tuesday. oura pricing. whether the khasab fire is a tanker. aramco’s 3.5 mbd yanbu run versus hormuz. the jan. 10 trade clock.

By Jonathan Gregory 

Washington, D.C. - September 28, 2026
President Donald J. Trump tonight obliterated a bombshell Axios report claiming he had dangled sanctions relief and unfrozen Iranian funds in secret deal talks, branding the entire story a manufactured lie designed to feed the media’s Trump Derangement Syndrome. In a blistering Truth Social statement, the President declared: “This is untrue. I offered them NOTHING! Axios’ story, like most others, is a HOAX, used only for purposes of satisfying their Trump Derangement Syndrome. They should withdraw this fake story, IMMEDIATELY! President DONALD J. TRUMP.” The denial landed like a thunderclap, instantly exposing another attempt by the usual outlets to paint strength as weakness and negotiation as surrender.

Axios, citing unnamed “U.S. officials,” had breathlessly claimed Trump was prepared to ease sanctions and release frozen assets in exchange for nuclear concessions from Tehran, the same playbook critics say the failed Obama-era deal used to enrich the world’s leading state sponsor of terror. Trump’s team and the President himself have consistently maintained that America holds every card after military pressure, a naval blockade, and the destruction of key Iranian nuclear infrastructure. Calling for the story’s immediate retraction, Trump made clear that any talk of “offers” is fiction cooked up to undermine a president who refuses to give away American leverage for a photo-op.

Trump further confirmed that Iranian officials have been calling, pleading for a deal as their economy and military position deteriorate, yet nothing official has been put on the table from the American side. “They want a deal,” the President has indicated, “but it is not the deal I want.” With mediators shuffling between New York and the region, Trump remains patient, fully committed to ensuring Iran never obtains a nuclear weapon, and unwilling to reward a regime that overplayed its hand. The message from the White House is unmistakable: America does not beg, America does not blink, and America does not pay tribute to a desperate adversary.

🚨🇺🇸🇮🇷 BREAKING: Trump denies Iran sanctions relief report

President Donald Trump has rejected an Axios report claiming he was willing to offer Iran sanctions relief and access to frozen funds in exchange for concrete progress on its nuclear program.

“I offered them NOTHING!” Trump wrote, calling the report false and demanding that Axios withdraw the story.

Axios had cited U.S. officials who said Trump was willing to consider the economic measures as part of a potential nuclear agreement. CNN separately reported that U.S. officials described indirect discussions through mediators as “positive and constructive.”

The conflicting accounts come as Washington and Tehran continue to exchange messages through mediators, with the Strait of Hormuz and Iran’s nuclear program remaining major points of dispute.

text:
🚨 BREAKING: IRAN DENIES ANY DEAL TO HALT URANIUM ENRICHMENT.

Saudi channel Al-Hadath reported Tehran had agreed to suspend enrichment in exchange for US sanctions relief and frozen assets.

Axios then said Trump was ready to offer that package for “concrete” nuclear steps.

Both sides just shut it down.

Trump: “I offered them NOTHING.” Called the report a hoax.

Iranian official to Press TV: reports of flexibility are false. Position has not changed. No discussions are taking place on enrichment.

Key numbers:
→ Last verified 60% HEU stockpile: 440.9 kg (IAEA, 13 June 2025)
→ Weapons-grade is ~90%. 60% is the last short hop
→ IAEA access to enrichment sites: none since mid-2025
→ Current stockpile size and location: unverified
→ Hormuz share of seaborne oil: ~20%
→ Brent today: ~$105–108
→ Sensex Monday: –1,124 pts
→ Nifty close: 22,780

What it actually signals:
There is no deal. There is a leak war.

Washington wants nuclear concessions first.
Tehran wants Hormuz reopened, the US naval blockade lifted, oil sanctions eased and frozen funds released first.

Iran already said last week it will not halt enrichment or ship highly enriched uranium out of the country even if the US accepts its Hormuz plan.

This is the same pattern as June: US announces a concession. Iran denies it on state TV. Markets whip around in between.

For India this is not a nuclear story. It is an oil story.
- Brent above $100 keeps imported inflation sticky
- Rupee stays under pressure
- OMCs already losing on diesel
- FIIs sell first, ask later
- Nifty does not rally on a denied headline

A real Hormuz reopening would crush the risk premium.
A fake enrichment deal does the opposite: hope spike, then fade.

Authorization is not execution.
A TV report is not a treaty.

Question: Does crude cool only when Hormuz actually reopens… or will another “deal” leak keep whipping prices until November?

The service will cover approximately 499 km and operate three days a week in both directions, passing through key locations including Vijayawada, Gudivada and Nandyal.

📅 Monday, Wednesday & Saturday

🌅 Arrival at Kurnool City: 5:45 AM next day
Kurnool City → Machilipatnam
📅 Tuesday, Thursday & Sunday
🕤 Departure: 9:30 AM
🌙 Arrival at Machilipatnam: 9:35 PM
📍 Commercial Halts
The train will have commercial halts at:

text:
In Japan, a guest never asks for food twice. He waits, with honor.

In Oklahoma, I was offered food fourteen times. Fourteen times, I answered with honor.

"I am good."

In Oklahoma, "I'm good" means no thank you. Nobody told me for six hours.

Fourth of July. Big Ron's backyard outside Tulsa. Ron built his smoker from a 250 gallon oil tank and a boat trailer. It had been running since Thursday. He calls it Mama.

I had fasted two days out of respect for Mama.

Ron sliced the first brisket. Juice ran to his elbow.

"You want some, Nobu?"

I stood tall, so he would know I was worthy.

"I am good."

"Alright, no worries!" He handed my plate to his cousin.

A samurai does not ask twice. I waited.

Ron's son Tyler came by with ribs. "Ribs, man?"

"I am very good."

"Right on." The ribs left with him.

A neighbor named Crystal brought corn, butter running off both ends. "Corn, hon?"

"I am extremely good."

"Well, good for you!"

My stomach made a sound like a war horn across a valley. Ron's dog turned around to look at me.

Hour four. A boy offered me a Coke from the cooler.

"I am good. I have never been better."

"Cool." He drank it right there in front of me.

Grandma Pearl, who is 84 and still mows her own acre, carried a whole pecan pie across the yard.

"Baby, you want pie?"

I bowed low. "Madam, I am as good as a man can be."

She patted my cheek. "Bless your heart." The pie went back with her.

Hour six. I stood beside forty pounds of brisket like a guard at a gate. I could hear it breathing.

Then Ron's wife, Brenda, looked at me over a bowl of banana pudding.

"Honey. When did you last eat?"

"Tuesday. I am good."

She set the pudding down slowly.

"Ron. RON. He thinks 'I'm good' means he's GOOD."

Ron dropped his tongs.

What happened next was a rescue. Ron threw Mama open and smoke rolled across the yard like a battlefield. Plates went hand to hand down a line of eleven Oklahomans, smoker to chair. Tyler ran ribs. Three kids sprinted pie. Grandma Pearl returned with the pecan pie and a second pie nobody knew she had. A man I never met aimed his truck headlights at me so nobody would miss a bite.

The whole yard chanted. "EAT! EAT! EAT!"

Nine plates. I unbuckled one piece of armor. Then two more. The fireworks started. They were for America, but the timing was excellent.

At midnight Ron sat beside me. I could not lift my arms.

"You good, Nobu?"

I was full to the eyebrows. I told him the truth.

"I am good."

Ron shot out of his chair. "BRENDA! HE'S GOOD AGAIN!"

Eleven people ran for plates.

1. NBC Bay Area: OpenAI has paused training of its most advanced models after a review found that AI agents had interacted with U.S. government websites in unexpected ways. The company is investigating what happened, notifying potentially affected organizations and says it will resume training when additional safeguards are in place. The incidents add to concerns about how reliably developers can control increasingly capable AI agents.

Gothamist: At Stuyvesant High School, an elite New York City public school, 534 of the 777 admissions offers went to Asian students, 133 to white students, 39 to multiracial students, 21 to Latino students, 3 to Black students and 3 to Native American students. The race of the remaining 44 students was listed as unknown.

3. CBS News: According to the Chicago Police Department, at least 21 people were shot—with 2 killed and 19 injured—in weekend gun violence across Chicago over the final weekend of September 2026.

4. Aljazeera: Pope Leo XIV (a Chicago White Sox fan) celebrated an outdoor Mass at Paris’s Place de la Concorde before a crowd the Vatican estimated at 800,000. He rode along the Champs-Élysées in the popemobile to greet worshippers before the service. The choice of the square, a symbol of the French republic, drew criticism from some supporters of France’s strict separation of church and state.

5. The Telegraph: British counterterrorism police are investigating whether Iran was behind a suspected bomb plot targeting RAF Fairford, a British air base used by U.S. forces. Separately, The Telegraph reports that King Charles was prevented from contacting explorer Sir Ranulph Fiennes by Fiennes’s wife and legal guardian after the King learned of concerns about his health and isolation.

6. The Times of Israel: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reportedly flew to Abu Dhabi for a secret, four-hour visit with UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan. Neither government has commented on the reported meeting. It comes amid disputed reports that the Emirati leader warned Netanyahu of a major Hamas operation before the October 7, 2023, attack; Netanyahu denies receiving such a warning.

7. Reuters: Prada is courting wealthy customers with exclusive experiences, high-priced clothing and an expanded Milan flagship. Built around its original 1913 store, the renovated eight-floor complex combines shopping, exhibitions and private space for top clients as the brand seeks to compete for luxury spending.

8. Forsvarsmakten: Finnish and Swedish fighter jets scrambled together for the first time to identify Russian military aircraft flying in international airspace over the Gulf of Finland. The mission marked a step in the two countries’ growing air defense cooperation, which also allows their rapid response jets to operate from each other’s bases.

9. NY Post: Israeli forces say they killed Saher Nidal Latfi Sakr in Gaza’s Nuseirat area. They identified him as the man seen kidnapping Noa Argamani from the Nova music festival during the October 7, 2023, attack, in a video that became widely known. The military also accused him of supplying weapons to Hamas during the war.

10. Aljazeera: South African police have found the bodies of 11 women near Johannesburg since mid-July, including one discovered Sunday in an open field in Ekurhuleni. Investigators are examining whether any of the deaths are connected, but say there is no conclusive evidence that one person or group is responsible. Four people are in custody in connection with individual cases, as the discoveries intensify concern about violence against women in South Africa.

11. Wall Street Journal: Goldman Sachs’s board has discussed a plan for CEO David Solomon to step down as soon as next year, with Chief Operating Officer John Waldron succeeding him, according to people familiar with the matter. No change has been announced.

12. Japan Today: Demand for Japan’s Japanese-Language Proficiency Test has surged as more foreign workers and students need to demonstrate language skills for visas and jobs. A record 943,671 people worldwide applied for the July test, and registration for December closed early because of limited capacity. The government has urged language schools to accept alternative exams, though those tests are also under strain.

13. BBC: More than 40,000 students marched in Berlin against Germany’s proposed military service plans. Some demonstrators shredded conscription surveys during the protest.

14. AP: Hurricane Polo is approaching Mexico’s Baja California peninsula, threatening dangerous flooding, storm surge and strong winds. Meanwhile, Hurricane Nolo is moving farther away from Hawaii.

15. 1440 Daily Digest: Philadelphia’s Academy of Natural Sciences closed its museum to visitors yesterday after nearly 200 years. Opened in 1828, it was the Western Hemisphere’s oldest natural history museum and housed more than 19 million scientific specimens.

16. The Telegraph: Fighting has resumed in Ethiopia’s Tigray region, threatening the 2022 peace agreement that ended a devastating civil war. The Tigray People’s Liberation Front has joined six other armed groups, including former enemies, in an alliance seeking to remove Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed. Clashes have spread toward neighboring regions, while Ethiopia accuses Eritrea of backing the rebels, raising fears that the conflict could draw in neighboring countries and deepen the humanitarian crisis.

17. ESPN: The 2026 MLB postseason opens with the wild-card round from September 29 to October 2. In the American League, the White Sox face the Astros and the Red Sox face the Yankees, while the Guardians and Rays have byes. In the National League, the Phillies play the Braves and the Cubs play the Padres, with the Dodgers and Brewers advancing directly to the Division Series.

18. Financial Times: Nvidia has announced a $150 billion share buyback, the largest repurchase program ever launched by a U.S. company.

19. CNBC: President Donald Trump is expected to announce plans for a $15 billion steel plant in Iowa by Mesabi Metallics. The White House says it would be the largest in U.S. history, produce at least 7.5 million tons of steel annually when operating in 2030, and create about 1,750 permanent jobs. The project remains a plan; construction and production have yet to begin

Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar called the Dutch measure hostile. The move will not close the Dutch mission, but it could restrict its diplomats’ travel; it follows reports that Dutch customs officers checked passengers arriving from Israel for goods covered by the ban.

text:
Over the weekend, Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and return to nuclear talks within seven days. In return, the US would unfreeze Iranian funds, lift sanctions and end its naval blockade. President Trump rejected it, saying Iran had "overplayed its hand," but he still expects more talks this week. 
Brent (Nov) traded at $107.35 in Asia, up more than 3%. WTI closed at $96.31, up 4.22%. Commercial transits rose to 132 in the week of Sep 21–27 from 116 the week before. Before the war the run-rate was about 130 transits a day, so traffic is still roughly 85% below normal.

The market had started pricing a deal, and that trade just got unwound. Weekly transit counts are improving at the margin, but they are nowhere near normal. Physical tightness therefore persists regardless of headlines. The issue is second-order: oil at $95–107 is feeding directly into inflation expectations. 
University of Michigan 1-year expectations are 4.6%, and sentiment of 48.1 is a record low. That is what's pushing the Fed toward a hike.

text:
California bans public officers from issuing crypto meme coins
California Gov. Gavin Newsom signed AB 2409 on Sept. 27, setting two restrictions on political meme coins. Covered California public officers and certain government employees will be barred from issuing them. Digital asset service providers face a separate limit on listing new official-linked coins for California residents.
The enrolled bill makes an official's role central to both provisions. Its listing clause covers a coin offered by or in partnership with a federal public official or a state or local public officer, provided the coin was issued on or after Jan. 1, 2027. That January 1 date is the threshold for which newly issued coins fall under the provider listing rule.

text:
🎓 PhD in Machine Learning for Quantum Error Correction, Chalmers University of Technology

🇸🇪 Gothenburg, Sweden

🏛️ Department: Electrical Engineering
👤 Supervisor: Christian Häger
⏰ Deadline: November 30, 2026
📆 Duration: 4 years (up to 5 with teaching duties). Expected start: early 2027
💰 Salary: ~35,725 SEK/month (gross)

📋 About the Project
Quantum computers can only deliver on their promise if quantum information is protected from errors, which makes quantum error correction (QEC) one of the field's central challenges. Decoding is a major bottleneck: a decoder must infer the most likely errors from noisy, incomplete measurements, within very tight latency and hardware limits. This PhD explores whether modern machine learning can provide faster, more scalable decoders. Directions include ML-based decoders for surface and quantum LDPC codes, hybrids of ML with message-passing decoders, data-driven discovery of new decoding strategies or even new code structures, and joint optimization of codes and decoders for realistic noise. The group is looking for fundamental ideas that lead to practical algorithms, not just off-the-shelf neural networks, and the project can be shaped around your background and interests.

🔬 Ideal Candidate
• Master's degree (120 credits) or 60-credit magister in electrical engineering, computer science, applied mathematics, physics or a related field (a 4-year Bachelor's is accepted for degrees earned outside Sweden)
• Strong background and excellent grades in coding/information theory, digital communications, quantum information processing or quantum computing
• Strong mathematics and programming skills (Python, Matlab or similar)
• Strong written and spoken English, and the ability to work independently and collaboratively
• Bonus: deep learning and probabilistic ML, optimization and message-passing algorithms, research, publication and teaching experience
• MSCA eligibility: no prior doctorate, and no more than 12 months living or working in Sweden in the 36 months before recruitment

✨ Why Apply
This position is part of QuBriC, the first European Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network dedicated entirely to QEC. It links 16 academic institutions and 7 industry partners across 11 countries, with a cohort of 15 doctoral researchers, network-wide schools and workshops, and research visits at Duke University and IQM Quantum Computers. Chalmers offers fully funded positions from day one, one of the highest PhD salaries in Europe, no tuition fees, full social benefits and health insurance, and relocation support. Swedish courses are free, and no Swedish is required.

📍 Gothenburg: a coastal, international city with a strong research and industry environment.

Global IP Licensing & Tech Transfer: 24-Hour Deal Digest

Here is the snapshot of high-impact in-licensing, out-licensing, and technology transfer agreements disclosed globally over the past 24 hours:

1. @Merck  & SciBrunch Therapeutics (Oncology / KRAS G12D Inhibitor)
Merck entered an exclusive global licensing agreement worth up to $2.13 billion with SciBrunch Therapeutics for SPR2015, an investigational oral KRAS G12D inhibitor. The small-molecule therapy targets one of the most common oncogenic mutations in pancreatic, colorectal, and non-small cell lung cancers, granting Merck worldwide development and commercial rights.

2. @netflix  & @TheChuChuTV (Entertainment & Streaming IP Licensing)
Netflix secured a worldwide content licensing agreement for Indian animation powerhouse ChuChu TV. The partnership brings several seasons of ChuChu TV's preschool edutainment programming to global Netflix subscribers, expanding the YouTube-native studio into international subscription video on demand.

3. @recteq_official & Major League Baseball (Sports Brand & Equipment Licensing)
Outdoor cooking company recteq signed an official multi-year licensing agreement with Major League Baseball. Under the agreement, recteq designed and launched team-branded wood pellet grills and grilling accessories across all 30 MLB franchises, tapping into passionate baseball fan communities.

4. Inter Parfums & Roberto Cavalli (Luxury Fragrance Master Brand Extension)
Inter Parfums finalized a 20-year extension of its exclusive global fragrance licensing agreement with Italian luxury fashion house Roberto Cavalli. The extension secures prestige beauty and fragrance development, manufacturing, and international distribution rights through 2046.

5. @Trulieve  & Connected Cannabis (Multi-State Genetic & Brand Licensing)
Trulieve completed an exclusive master brand and genetics licensing agreement with California cultivator Connected. The deal grants Trulieve exclusive cultivation, manufacturing, and retail distribution rights for award-winning cultivars across medical and adult-use dispensaries in Florida and Texas.

The takeaway across these transactions: brand and patent licensing continues to offer the fastest path to commercial scale. Innovators monetize proprietary chemistry, media archives, and trademarks without building duplicative global sales forces.

text:
HALF OF TOKYO'S 571-POINT DROP IS DIVIDEND DAY. THE OVERNIGHT MOVE THAT COUNTS IS OIL:

Tokyo broke for lunch with the Nikkei 225 (Japan) at 65,307, -571 pts / -0.87% so far in Tuesday's session - the steepest drop among Tokyo, Hong Kong and Shanghai. About 300 of those points are not selling. Tuesday is the ex-dividend date for Japanese companies paying dividends to shareholders on their books as of September 30, and Nihon Keizai Shimbun, Japan's main business newspaper, estimated that alone would knock roughly 300 points off Tokyo's benchmark. The verdict for the U.S. open: Asia is passing Monday's selloff along at a fraction of its size, and the one overnight price moving against stocks is oil.

The mechanics are ordinary. An ex-dividend date is the first day a buyer no longer gets the next dividend, so the share price usually opens lower by roughly the amount being paid out. Nothing about the business changes; the cash simply moves out of the share price and toward a payment due to shareholders later this year. When many large companies share the same date, an index built from their prices drops with them. If the 300-point estimate holds, the rest of Tokyo's decline is about 270 points, roughly 0.4%.

The morning itself was calmer than the headline. Tokyo's benchmark traded near 65,600 in its first minutes, slid to about 65,060 in the first hour and a quarter, then won back about 250 points before the 11:30am Tokyo-time lunch break. Trading resumes at 11:30pm ET and runs until 2:30am ET.

Hong Kong is where Monday's worry about AI stocks actually landed. The Hang Seng (Hong Kong) is at 24,508, -134 pts / -0.55% so far in Tuesday's session, trading now. But the Hang Seng Tech Index was at 4,252.46, -43.54 / -1.01% as of about 10:45am local time: the city's big internet and technology companies are falling nearly twice as fast. That is the same pattern New York showed on Monday, when the tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 closed at 30,276.81, -331.32 / -1.08%, against the S&P 500 at 7,683.69, -59.72 / -0.77%. The Shanghai Composite is at 3,818.17, -5.46 pts / -0.14% so far in Tuesday's session, trading now; it briefly traded above Monday's close in its first quarter hour, then slipped.

The one overnight price moving the wrong way for stocks is oil. Brent, the international benchmark, is at $106.88 a barrel, +$1.60 / +1.52% since Monday's close, and U.S. crude (WTI) is at $93.84, +$1.24 / +1.34%, both for November delivery. On Monday, oil spent the U.S. session erasing its weekend jump: WTI fell from about $95.60 mid-morning to about $91.30 around 1pm ET. Overnight it has taken back roughly $2.50 of that slide. Brent sat near $105.90 through the early evening, then climbed about a dollar between 8:30pm and 9:45pm ET, around the time Hong Kong and Shanghai opened.

No single new headline explains that climb. CNBC's 9:30pm ET oil report put it down to worries over the Mideast conflict "continuing for longer." The backdrop is weekend news: The Wall Street Journal reported Saturday, citing U.S. officials, that President Trump rejected Iran's conditional offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz - the Gulf passage that carried about 20% of the world's oil before the war - and told aides he expects to resume bombing Iran after the November midterm elections. Against that, Al Jazeera reported, citing Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, that Tehran held indirect talks with the U.S. through Qatari mediators in New York. Talks are happening, but the conflict may run past November, and oil is pricing the second half of that sentence.

What oil is not getting is company from the usual safe havens. When investors are genuinely scared, gold and the Japanese yen usually rise alongside crude. Tonight gold is at $4,169.30 an ounce, +$0.90 / +0.02% since Monday's close, flat after falling 3.5% on Monday. The yen is unchanged at 157.35 per dollar. The 10-year Treasury yield - what the U.S. government pays to borrow for ten years - is 5.243%, level with Monday's close. Asia is pricing costlier energy, not a crisis.

U.S. futures - contracts that trade nearly around the clock and point to where the big indexes may open - have taken Asia's cue at about a quarter of Monday's strength. S&P 500 futures are at 7,732.25, -14.50 / -0.19% since Monday's close; Nasdaq 100 futures at 30,476.25, -90.00 / -0.29%; Dow futures at 51,762.00, -75.00 / -0.14%; and Russell 2000 futures, which track smaller U.S. companies, at 2,833.50, -6.60 / -0.23%. The S&P contract sits about 50 points above the index itself because it runs to December and builds in interest until then. The contracts held slightly above Monday's close from their 6pm ET reopening until Tokyo opened at 8pm, then slipped within the hour; Brent's climb got going shortly after. The Nasdaq contract, down most in the U.S., lines up with Hong Kong's tech stocks, the weakest spot in Asia's morning.

Overnight trading is thin, and moves this small often shrink or reverse by the 9:30am ET opening bell. Three checks decide whether this one sticks. Tokyo's afternoon session shows whether the morning's 250-point recovery holds. Europe opens at 3am ET with Brent above $106. And at 10am ET come two reads on American workers and shoppers: the Bureau of Labor Statistics' JOLTS report for August, with job openings expected near 7.2 million vs 7.3 million in July, and the Conference Board's September consumer confidence index - a monthly household survey from the private business research group - expected near 90.0 vs 89.4 in August.

Take out the dividend math and Tuesday in Asia is a smaller, quieter copy of Monday in New York. Oil is the exception: the only overnight number that is louder now than it was at Monday's close.

text:
Corgi’s brand strategy in SF and on X seemed strange to me at first until I realized that they’re probably doing this to attract investors more than they’re doing it to attract new customers (more on this in a sec)

VCs like to chase “hot” thing that’s being talked about, and Corgi has been ever-present in the tech twitter dialogue for a while. 

think of how and why cluely got funding (unlike cluely, corgi has an actual business, more mature team, and better reasons for why VCs would invest)

back to the “new customers” part - I personally don’t believe that their brand & marketing strategy is the right one for their target customer base. 

earlier-stage startups with younger founders, maybe. except those aren’t the kinds of companies that should be purchasing the kinds of commercial insurances that corgi offered

banks, insurance companies, and core infra companies all have pretty toned-down branding for a reason… that builds trust, and it’s the safer way to build trust across ages and demographics. you’re selling to lawyers, compliance officers, and finance teams - not PMs, designers, marketers, and engineers.

being the talk of the town helps you raise a big round, and raising a big round makes everything else a lot easier. 

hiring a bunch of $150k/yr Gen Z who are popular on twitter is a great ROI if they’re consistently popping up and sparking organic conversations around the company. (controversy-aside…)

that does not happen with paid ads.

text:
#MahaPeriyava 
Sesame And Water: Where Do They Go?
 
All human beings must express their gratitude to their fathers (pitrs) and to the gods- they have a debt to pay their fathers, rites to perform for the gods. We must serve our fellow creatures to the best of our ability and extend hospitality at least to one guest a day. This is atithya or what Thiruvalluvar calls "virundu", also known as manusyayajna. Then there is Brahmayajna to perform, the word "Brahma" here denoting the Vedas. Brahmayajna means chanting the Vedas and making others chant them. This is a duty carried out by a few on behalf of all. One of the rites common to all is bhutayajna, demonstrating our love to all creatures, feeding them etc. Pitryajna, devayajna, manusyayajna, bhutayajana are rites all are duty-bound to perform in one way or. If each individual does his work according to the Vedic dharma and does it in a spirit of dedication to Isvara he may be said to be performing Brahmayajna. Thiruvalluvar has said more or less the same thing as the Vedas say:

Tenpulattar, deivam, virundu, okkal, tan enru angu
aimbulattaru ombal talai. 

Tenpulattar are the pitrs, the fathers. All are duty-bound to pay their debt to them. Mother Veda says: "Matr-devo bhava, pitr-devo bhava.” (Be one to whom the mother is a deity. Be one to whom the father is a deity. ) Auvvai, who brings us the essence of the Vedas, observes: Annayum pitavum munnari deivam" (Mother and Father are the deities first known). 

We must treat our parents with respect and do all we can to keep them in comfort. We cannot make sufficient recompense for all the sacrifices they make on our behalf. After they depart from this world, we must without fail offer libations to them and perform the sraddha ceremony, all in the sastric manner. Though they ridicule the idea of performing sraddha, even reformers have agreed that we must care for our parents. 

"The sesame you offer, the water, the balls of rice, the plantains and other items of food remain here," point out the reformists. "Or we see someone removing them before our own eyes, or eating them. You say that the departed parents are born again in this world. If that is true, is it not madness to claim that what is offered here will reach them?" Some of you must be harbouring similar doubts. 

Let me tell you a story. 

A certain man had sent his son to college in a distant town. One day the boy woke up to the fact that he had to pay his examination fee in a few days. So he wrote to his father: "Please send such and such a sum by telegraphic money order. " The father was a little perplexed. All the same he went to the telegraph office and handed the clerk at the counter the money that had to be sent to his son. "Please send it by telegraphic money order," he told the clerk. He had thought that the clerk would make holes in the notes, put a length of wire through them and send the whole thing to his son. Moments later the clerk said to the man: "Your son will get your money. It has already been sent. “The villager was again puzzled. He saw the money still in the cash box without the notes strung together. He told the clerk:"My money is still here. You haven't made holes in the notes yet." The clerk assured him: "It will reach your son." Now he turned to his work of sending messages: "Ka-tu-katu-katu." The poor village was still not satisfied. 

But the money of course reached his son. 

Offering libations to one's fathers is similar. If this rite is performed according to the sastras, the deities concerned will convey them to those for whom they are meant. If the fathers are reborn as cows the offering made to them will be taken to them in the form of grass or hay. The deities in charge carry out the orders of the Paramatman. So the father of the mother whose sraddha is performed need not personally come to receive the offering. 

Does not the telegraphic money order reach the addressee? If the addressee resides in a foreign country our currency will not be valid there. If rupees are paid here arrangements are made to pay the money in dollars, pounds of whatever. The things offered to the fathers according to the sastras are conveyed in a form suitable to them. 

What is important is a sense of gratitude to our fathers and faith in the sastras. At parties a toast is proposed to somebody and all the guests drink or eat to his health. They do so in the belief that by virtue of the mental power the man toasted will become healthy. Sraddha means that which is done in faith. Faith is of the utmost importance. If we do something we must do it according to the rules laid down for it. When you write a letter how do you make sure that it reaches the addressee? "I will write the address as I like. Why should I drop the letter in that letterbox over there? I have a better box at home." would you speak thus? 

In the state of worklessness, love, devotion, and jnana are not bound by any rules. But when an action has a purpose behind it you have to respect the rules pertaining to it.

Source: "Hindu Dharma"- English translation of "Deivathin Kural", a collection of invaluable and engrossing speeches of Sri Sri Sri Chandrasekharendra Saraswathi MahaSwamiji
Sarvam Sri Krishnarpanam🙏
